boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Emory University
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe evening food stops on the Atlanta campus or immediately beside it, with published closing times of 10 p.m. or later. Campus schedules can change during breaks.

cards.title: The 24-Hour Campus Bodega
cards.subtitle: Emory Student Center, ESC North second floor
cards.notes: Bring an EmoryCard for overnight Student Center access, then use the cashierless market for packaged food, drinks, or essentials.
cards.short_summary: A round-the-clock market inside Emory's student union.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory Dining identifies Eagle Emporium as an ESC North second-floor campus bodega open 24/7 through Just Walk Out technology.
cards.access_notes: The market is open 24/7; Emory says the Student Center requires an EmoryCard for student access overnight.

cards.title: The 11 P.M. Meal-Exchange Counter
cards.subtitle: Inside Eagle Emporium at the Emory Student Center
cards.notes: Go before the counter closes at 11 p.m.; use the surrounding Emporium afterward if you only need packaged food or drinks.
cards.short_summary: A staffed late counter within Emory's all-night market.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory's posted standard schedule lists Nom Station at Eagle Emporium from 11 a.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Posted standard hours are 11 a.m.–11 p.m.; schedules may change for academic breaks and holidays.

cards.title: Coffee by the One-A.M. Study Tables
cards.subtitle: Level 1 of Robert W. Woodruff Library
cards.notes: Check library entry rules before heading over, then choose a drink, pastry, sandwich, or salad without leaving the study building.
cards.short_summary: A library café paired with Emory's latest posted study-night hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory describes Banjo on Woodruff Library Level 1, and its posted schedule lists 1 a.m. closing on several standard-schedule nights.
cards.access_notes: Posted standard hours include closing at 1 a.m. Monday–Thursday and on weekend nights; library access rules still apply.

cards.title: Midnight at the Old Depot
cards.subtitle: One Eagle Row on Emory's Atlanta campus
cards.notes: Use the Friday or Saturday midnight window for coffee or food, and verify the day's schedule when classes are not in session.
cards.short_summary: A historic depot café with midnight weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory's posted standard schedule lists Kaldi's at The Depot until midnight on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Posted standard hours run until midnight Friday and Saturday; break and holiday hours may differ.

cards.entity_name: Woodruff Residential Center Late Night Dining
cards.title: The One-A.M. WREC Counter
cards.subtitle: Woodruff Residential Center on Emory's Atlanta campus
cards.notes: Head to WREC after the main dinner period and confirm the operating counter before ordering, since vendors can change by term.
cards.short_summary: Emory's explicitly designated late-night residential dining stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory Dining labels Woodruff Residential Center as a late-night dining location, and the posted standard schedule lists service until 1 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Posted standard hours are 6 p.m.–1 a.m. Monday–Thursday; academic-break schedules may differ.

cards.title: Ten-O'Clock Dinner at DCT
cards.subtitle: Emory Student Center South, first floor
cards.notes: Use the final evening service window for a full dining-hall meal, and check whether your meal plan or another tender is accepted.
cards.short_summary: Emory's main dining hall extends dinner service to 10 p.m. on select nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory identifies Dobbs Common Table as its all-you-care-to-eat dining hall, with posted standard hours extending to 10 p.m. Monday–Thursday and Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Posted standard hours extend to 10 p.m. Monday–Thursday and Sunday; break and holiday schedules may differ.

cards.title: The Ten-P.M. Clairmont Option
cards.subtitle: Clairmont Campus
cards.notes: Use this when your evening ends on Clairmont Campus; review the day's hours first and bring an accepted campus payment method.
cards.short_summary: Made-to-order evening food on Emory's Clairmont Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory says Clairmont Café serves made-to-order flatbreads, salads, burgers, and sandwiches; posted standard hours extend to 10 p.m. Monday–Thursday.
cards.access_notes: Posted standard hours are 11:30 a.m.–10 p.m. Monday–Thursday; academic-break hours may differ.

cards.title: Eleven O'Clock in Emory Village
cards.subtitle: 1569 North Decatur Road, beside campus
cards.notes: Walk into Emory Village for dine-in, patio, or takeout service; check the live location page before relying on the final hour.
cards.short_summary: An Indian kitchen beside campus with an 11 p.m. close.
cards.evidence_claim: Sankranti's official Emory Village location page lists the restaurant at 1569 North Decatur Road and shows daily hours through 11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: The official location page lists 11 a.m.–11 p.m. every day; confirm same-day hours before leaving campus.

cards.title: The Weeknight Ten-P.M. Bowl
cards.subtitle: 1556 North Decatur Road in Emory Village
cards.notes: Use the weekday closing window for a salad or warm bowl; weekends end earlier, so verify the day before walking over.
cards.short_summary: A campus-edge counter-service option open until 10 p.m. on weekdays.
cards.evidence_claim: Sweetgreen's official locations page lists Emory Village at 1556 North Decatur Road, open until 10 p.m. Monday through Friday.
cards.source_title: Sweetgreen Locations | Find a Restaurant Near You
cards.access_notes: Official hours are 10:30 a.m.–10 p.m. Monday–Friday and 10:30 a.m.–9 p.m. Saturday–Sunday.

cards.title: Friday-Night Pizza at Ten
cards.subtitle: 1577 North Decatur Road in Emory Village
cards.notes: Reserve or check availability before the Friday or Saturday closing hour; the restaurant is closed Sunday and ends earlier weekdays.
cards.short_summary: A sit-down Emory Village pizza and pasta stop for weekend evenings.
cards.evidence_claim: Double Zero's official site identifies the restaurant in Emory Village at 1577 North Decatur Road and lists Friday and Saturday service until 10 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Official hours are 5–10 p.m. Friday and Saturday, 5–9 p.m. Monday–Thursday, and closed Sunday.

warnings: Emory's posted campus schedule states that hours may change during academic breaks and holidays; verify same-day hours before traveling.
The Sankranti hours evidence is on the business's official development-host location page because its current production page did not expose the hours in searchable text.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten Emory spaces for quiet focus, group work, creative production, recreation, and community between classes.

cards.title: Settle Into the Matheson Reading Room
cards.subtitle: A high-ceilinged quiet room across the Level 3 bridge
cards.notes: Cross the Level 3 bridge from Woodruff Library, choose a large wooden table, and keep conversation for a group-study area.
cards.short_summary: Long tables, soft alcove seating, and a strict quiet expectation make this a focused reading destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory Libraries identifies the Matheson Reading Room as a designated quiet area with large wooden tables, chairs, sofas, and adjacent quiet rooms.
cards.source_title: Find a Quiet Study Area | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on Level 3 across the bridge in Candler Library; users are asked to maintain utmost quiet.

cards.title: Build a Work Session Around the Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Flexible study and production resources across Woodruff Library
cards.notes: Start on Levels 1 or 2 for collaborative work, then use a reservable room or specialized workstation when the project calls for it.
cards.short_summary: This multi-floor commons combines ordinary seating with computers, study rooms, printing, and production tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory states that the Learning Commons provides multiple floors of study rooms, workstations, printing resources, and furniture for individual or collaborative study.
cards.source_title: Learning Commons in Woodruff Library | Emory University
cards.access_notes: Located inside Woodruff Library at 540 Asbury Circle; availability follows Woodruff Library building hours.

cards.entity_name: Marian K. Heilbrun Music and Media Library
cards.title: Work With Sound and Images at Heilbrun
cards.subtitle: A media-focused library on Woodruff Level 4
cards.notes: Bring a media assignment here for format playback or computer work, and use the open seating areas for quieter individual study.
cards.short_summary: Heilbrun pairs wooded views and quiet tables with playback stations, media collections, and adjacent creative software.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory Libraries says Heilbrun occupies Level 4 of Woodruff Library and offers media collections, 41 listening and viewing stations, computers, and MediaLab access.
cards.source_title: Marian K. Heilbrun Music and Media Library | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Current Emory students, faculty, and staff may use its Learning Commons and MediaLab computers during business hours.

cards.title: Meet and Make on Cox Hall’s Second Floor
cards.subtitle: A technology lounge with workspaces and meeting rooms
cards.notes: Head upstairs from the food market, choose a workstation or lounge seat, and reserve a room when your group needs a defined workspace.
cards.short_summary: The second floor of Cox Hall supports both solo computer work and informal group meetups.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory describes Cox Hall’s second floor as home to lounges and the Computing Center, with computers, varied seating, and meeting rooms available to students.
cards.access_notes: Located on Cox Hall’s second floor; consult the linked Computing Center schedule because university holiday and activity hours vary.

cards.title: Take a Screen Break in the Rec Lounge
cards.subtitle: Games, billiards, and television on ESC South’s second floor
cards.notes: Drop in between classes for billiards or a video game, and check the RecRe lockers when your group needs controllers or board games.
cards.short_summary: This recreation lounge offers an indoor reset built around shared games rather than food or purchases.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory Student Center identifies the second-floor ESC South Rec Lounge as a place for pool, television, and video games, with games and controllers available through RecRe lockers.
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of Emory Student Center South; use is subject to student-center building access and event availability.

cards.title: Bring a Small Group to ESC North
cards.subtitle: A third-floor lounge with seating and screen mirroring
cards.notes: Use the third-floor seating for a casual meetup, and bring an HDMI-compatible device if your group wants to share material on a screen.
cards.short_summary: The North lounge is suited to low-key conversation and informal screen sharing between scheduled commitments.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory says the third-floor ESC North Lounge has comfortable seating and flat-screen televisions equipped with cable and HDMI screen-mirroring options.
cards.access_notes: Located on the third floor of Emory Student Center North; building access and lounge availability may change for events.

cards.title: Prototype an Idea at The Hatchery
cards.subtitle: Emory’s creativity and collaboration space at Emory Point
cards.notes: Bring an early-stage idea to the makerspace, use the available craft or fabrication tools, and ask staff about rooms for larger sessions.
cards.short_summary: The Hatchery gives student projects room to move from sketches and discussion into tangible prototypes.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory describes The Hatchery as a 15,000-square-foot creativity and collaboration space with an inclusive makerspace, classrooms, meeting rooms, and event space.
cards.access_notes: Located at 1578 Avenue Place, Suite 200; current posted hours vary between summer and fall/spring, and it is closed weekends.

cards.title: Find Collaborative Seating in the Science Commons
cards.subtitle: Atwood Chemistry Center’s central community hub
cards.notes: Use the varied seating for a study meetup near science classes, and move into one of the transparent meeting spaces when appropriate.
cards.short_summary: Atwood’s central commons mixes open seating, enclosed meeting areas, a library outpost, and a café.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory states that the Atwood Chemistry Center renovation created the Science Commons with meeting spaces, a library satellite, a coffee shop, and varied seating.
cards.source_title: Emerson Hall and the Atwood Chemistry Center
cards.access_notes: Located within the Atwood Chemistry Center; classroom, meeting-space, library, and café access may follow separate schedules.

cards.title: Choose a Quiet Table at Pitts
cards.subtitle: A theology library with public study areas and identity check-in
cards.notes: Bring focused reading rather than a video call, check in at the circulation desk, and follow the library’s no-food-and-drink policy.
cards.short_summary: Pitts offers a quieter academic setting with extensive collections and controlled but visitor-friendly entry.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitts states that it is an Emory professional library open to Emory patrons and checked-in visitors; its public spaces permit study but not online classes or calls.
cards.access_notes: Bring a valid Emory ID; visitors must show photo identification and check in. Online classes, calls, food, and drinks are not allowed.

cards.title: Shift to a Quieter Health Sciences Study Space
cards.subtitle: Individual and group study resources near Emory’s health schools
cards.notes: Use open seating for quiet work, or book an individual or group room when a health-sciences project needs privacy or collaboration.
cards.short_summary: This library broadens the study-space map beyond central campus with quieter seating and reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory’s student academic toolkit lists Woodruff Health Sciences Center Library among quieter open-seating locations and among libraries offering study rooms to students.
cards.access_notes: Open seating and reservable rooms are separate options; check the library’s current access rules and reservation system before visiting.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten admission-free museum, gallery, archive, observatory, and historic-site outings for Emory students around Atlanta.

cards.title: Compare Ancient Art at the Carlos
cards.subtitle: Bring your Emory ID for a free gallery afternoon
cards.notes: Meet in the rotunda, choose two collection galleries, and compare one object each before regrouping for the Sunday public tour.
cards.short_summary: An Emory-ID outing through collections spanning Africa, the ancient Mediterranean, the Americas, and Asia.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum lists free admission for Emory students and for all college and university students with valid ID.
cards.source_title: Hours and Admission | Emory Carlos Museum
cards.access_notes: Show a valid Emory or other college ID. Open Tuesday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday noon–5 p.m.; closed Mondays and university holidays.

cards.entity_name: Stuart A. Rose Manuscript, Archives, and Rare Book Library
cards.title: Request an Archive Show-and-Tell
cards.subtitle: Explore primary sources together on Woodruff Library’s tenth floor
cards.notes: Pick a shared theme, request materials at least five days ahead, and compare discoveries around the reading-room table.
cards.short_summary: A planned group encounter with rare books, manuscripts, photographs, and archival collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose Library states that use of its collections in the reading room is free and open to the public, without special permission or introduction letters.
cards.source_title: Preparing for a Research Visit | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Appointments and material requests must be made five calendar days in advance. Reading-room appointments are Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.

cards.title: Solve Public-Health Mysteries at the CDC Museum
cards.subtitle: Walk through permanent and changing exhibitions beside campus
cards.notes: Reserve the same entry window, bring the required identification, and trade observations in the permanent Story of CDC gallery.
cards.short_summary: A group museum visit connecting disease-detective work, CDC history, technology, and public health.
cards.evidence_claim: The CDC states that its museum is free and open to the public, with both permanent and changing exhibitions.
cards.source_title: David J. Sencer CDC Museum | CDC
cards.access_notes: Reservations are required. Adults over 18 need government-issued REAL ID; non-U.S. citizens need a passport. Open weekdays 9 a.m.–4 p.m., excluding federal holidays.

cards.title: Run a Free Science-Hall Scavenger Hunt
cards.subtitle: Explore hands-on displays at the DeKalb school system’s science center
cards.notes: Choose three exhibit themes, split into pairs to find an example of each, then reconvene outside to share the strongest explanation.
cards.short_summary: A purchase-free science outing through exhibits and the center’s associated grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: Fernbank Science Center states that general admission is free and includes its exhibit hall and associated grounds.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current operating hours before leaving. The planetarium is separately ticketed, so keep this hang to the free exhibit hall and grounds.

cards.title: Share a Telescope View After Dark
cards.subtitle: Join a weather-dependent public observation near Emory
cards.notes: Call before departure, arrive before the line cutoff, and have everyone note one detail seen through the 36-inch telescope.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost evening of public telescope viewing at Fernbank Science Center’s observatory.
cards.evidence_claim: Fernbank Science Center documents free public observations on Thursday and Friday evenings when weather permits.
cards.access_notes: Viewing is Thursday and Friday evenings, weather permitting. August–October hours are 8:30–10 p.m.; call 678-874-7102 about 30 minutes before opening.

cards.entity_name: Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park
cards.title: Walk the King Historic District
cards.subtitle: Connect exhibits, Ebenezer Baptist Church, and Auburn Avenue landmarks
cards.notes: Start at the temporary visitor center, choose a self-guided route, and pause together to discuss one site that reframes Atlanta history.
cards.short_summary: A fee-free civil-rights history walk through museum exhibits and preserved neighborhood landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that no entrance fee or pass is required for Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park.
cards.source_title: Fees & Passes - Martin Luther King, Jr. National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: Begin at the temporary visitor center at 39 Boulevard NE. Check current conditions because individual buildings and ranger-led Birth Home tours may be unavailable.

cards.title: Tour Georgia’s Capitol Together
cards.subtitle: Follow a free route through government, portraits, and state history
cards.notes: Download the tour brochure, assign each person a floor or artifact to track, and compare findings beneath the Capitol’s historic dome.
cards.short_summary: A free self-guided or scheduled group tour incorporating the Capitol Museum and Hall of Valor.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries states that all Capitol tours, including the Capitol Museum and Hall of Valor, are free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Self-guided tours require no reservation and run Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m., except state holidays. Groups of 25 or more should call ahead.

cards.title: Trace Atlanta Stories at Oakland
cards.subtitle: Take a respectful self-guided walk through history and horticulture
cards.notes: Download the free digital guide, select a compact route, and photograph architectural or botanical details without disturbing memorials.
cards.short_summary: A free, self-paced walk among Oakland’s gardens, monuments, historic roads, and burial sections.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Oakland Foundation states that Oakland Cemetery is free to visit and that no entrance fee is charged.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit to Oakland Cemetery | Top Atlanta Attraction
cards.access_notes: Cemetery grounds are open dawn to dusk. Standard entry is free, but guided tours, fundraising events, and visitor parking may cost money.

cards.title: Trade Takes on Contemporary Art
cards.subtitle: Use free admission for a conversation-led gallery hang
cards.notes: Pair up for separate galleries, select one work that invites debate, then regroup and explain the choices without trying to reach consensus.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission gallery visit centered on current contemporary-art exhibitions and group discussion.
cards.evidence_claim: Atlanta Contemporary’s 2025–2028 strategic plan states that the institution offers free admission every day.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; verify current exhibition dates and public hours directly with Atlanta Contemporary before traveling. Registration or donations may be optional.

cards.title: Follow Money from Barter to the Vault
cards.subtitle: Explore currency, banking, and cash processing in Midtown
cards.notes: Take the self-guided route in a small group, compare favorite currency artifacts, and watch the automated cash-processing area together.
cards.short_summary: A completely free museum outing through money history, interactive economics displays, and a working-bank overlook.
cards.evidence_claim: The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta states that the Atlanta Monetary Museum is entirely free.
cards.source_title: Atlanta Monetary Museum - Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta
cards.access_notes: Groups under 10 may visit without scheduling Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m., except federal holidays. Entry includes security screening; museum parking is unavailable.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Emory study environments, from silent reading rooms and open science seating to reservable solo and group rooms.

cards.title: Settle In Under Matheson’s High Ceilings
cards.subtitle: A designated quiet room across the Level 3 bridge
cards.notes: Bring quiet work and use the large tables or alcove seating; voices carry easily beneath the room’s high ceilings.
cards.short_summary: A formal reading room for focused, low-noise study at long wooden tables or in upholstered alcoves.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory identifies Matheson Reading Room as a designated quiet area with large wooden tables and chairs or sofas in two alcoves.
cards.source_title: Find a Quiet Study Area | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on Level 3 across the bridge in Candler Library; Emory requests the utmost quiet in this room. Use is subject to Woodruff Library building access and hours.

cards.entity_name: Marian K. Heilbrun Music and Media Library
cards.title: Work Beside the Wooded Views at Heilbrun
cards.subtitle: Quiet tables and media stations on Woodruff Level 4
cards.notes: Choose a large table for reading or a media station for audiovisual work while keeping conversation out of this quiet area.
cards.short_summary: A quiet library environment combining substantial tables, comfortable chairs, media stations, and woodland views.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory lists Heilbrun Music and Media Library as a designated quiet area with large wooden tables, comfortable chairs, and media viewing stations.
cards.source_title: Find a Quiet Study Area | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on Level 4 of the Woodruff Library Building. Use is subject to library access rules and current building hours.

cards.title: Take a Computer Carrel Across from ECDS
cards.subtitle: Specialized workstations and large tables on Woodruff Level 3
cards.notes: Use a workstation carrel for computer-based assignments or spread materials across a large table; keep conversation subdued.
cards.short_summary: A quiet-leaning Level 3 workspace with individual computer carrels and larger shared work surfaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory states that the space across from the Emory Center for Digital Scholarship has individual carrels with computer workstations and large tables.
cards.source_title: Find a Quiet Study Area | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on Level 3 across from ECDS. Loud conversation is discouraged; access follows Woodruff Library building hours and policies.

cards.title: Study in the Atwood Chemistry Atrium
cards.subtitle: An open science-library setting with individual and group seating
cards.notes: Use the atrium seating for individual work or a group session, with printing and scanning available through the branch library.
cards.short_summary: A sunlit branch-library environment inside Atwood Chemistry Center with flexible seating and practical study services.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory describes Science Commons as a branch library in the Atwood Chemistry Center atrium and depicts individual seating and group meeting spaces.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Level 2 atrium of Atwood Chemistry Center. The Science Commons page lists regular building hours as Monday–Friday, 7 a.m.–7 p.m., with weekends closed; verify exceptions before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Goizueta Business Library Group Study Spaces
cards.title: Connect the Team at Goizueta’s Study Tables
cards.subtitle: Reservable monitor-and-whiteboard tables for Goizueta students
cards.notes: Bring at least three teammates, reserve ahead, and connect a laptop to the wall monitor for shared notes or presentation review.
cards.short_summary: Two technology-equipped group tables designed for collaborative business-school assignments.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory documents two Goizueta Business Library group-study tables, each with a wall-mounted monitor and whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to Goizueta Business School students. Reservations have a two-hour maximum and require at least three people.

cards.entity_name: MacMillan Law Library Student Study Rooms
cards.title: Reserve Uninterrupted Time at MacMillan
cards.subtitle: Ten reservable rooms for solo or group law study
cards.notes: Book up to three days ahead for uninterrupted individual or group work, keeping the daily two-hour allowance in mind.
cards.short_summary: A set of ten rooms within the law library for concentrated solo sessions or small-group collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory Law states that MacMillan Law Library has ten student study rooms available for uninterrupted solo or group study.
cards.source_title: Reserving Library Space | Emory University School of Law
cards.access_notes: Rooms are limited to law students, reservable up to three days ahead, and capped at two hours per student in each 24-hour period.

cards.entity_name: Woodruff Library Short-term Individual Study Rooms
cards.title: Close the Door for a Solo Work Block
cards.subtitle: Private reservable rooms with a desk, chair, shelves, and power
cards.notes: Reserve one for an interview, test, virtual meeting, or focused solo task; use headphones because the rooms are not soundproof.
cards.short_summary: Compact private rooms furnished for short, solitary sessions that need fewer visual and conversational distractions.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory says these one-person rooms include a desk, chair, bookshelves, and power outlet and support private short-term work.
cards.source_title: Individual Study Rooms and Carrels | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available to Emory students for one-person use. Reserve up to 14 days ahead for no more than three hours per day; rooms are private but not soundproof.

cards.title: Match the Room to the Group Project
cards.subtitle: Reservable rooms with and without technology across Woodruff
cards.notes: Check the room equipment before booking, then reserve a space suited to discussion, screen sharing, or collaborative review.
cards.short_summary: A distributed collection of enclosed group rooms offering both technology-equipped and simpler configurations.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory states that Woodruff Library has group study rooms throughout the building, including rooms with and without technology.
cards.access_notes: Advance reservation requirements and room-specific rules apply. Building maps place group study rooms on Level 4 and in the Stacks Tower.

cards.title: Find a Carrel Among the Bookstacks
cards.subtitle: Individual quiet-study seats on Stacks Tower Levels 4, 5, and 8
cards.notes: Choose an unoccupied wall carrel for individual work, stay quiet, and be ready to move if the carrel’s assigned user arrives.
cards.short_summary: Individual desks placed near the collections for quiet reading and writing with fewer group-work distractions.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory documents individual wall carrels in the bookstacks on Levels 4, 5, and 8 and permits use of vacant assigned carrels conditionally.
cards.source_title: Find a Quiet Study Area | Emory Libraries
cards.access_notes: Group conversation is discouraged. A user occupying an assigned carrel must vacate it if the assignee arrives; library access rules apply.

cards.title: Build a Tech-Ready Session at Cox Hall
cards.subtitle: Computer workstations plus reservable meeting and study rooms
cards.notes: Start at a workstation for digital assignments or reserve a room when the work calls for discussion, rehearsal, or shared screens.
cards.short_summary: A campus computing environment that supports both workstation-based individual work and reservable collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory lists computer workstations and bookable meeting or study rooms among the Computing Center at Cox Hall’s student spaces.
cards.access_notes: Room booking and center access requirements apply. Consult the Computing Center’s current schedule before visiting because operating hours and classroom availability can change.

warnings: Current hours can change for academic breaks, exams, holidays, and building exceptions; consult the linked official location pages before visiting.
Coordinates and maps URLs are null because card-level coordinates or canonical map URLs were not verified from the cited direct sources.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along corridors in Emory’s practical off-campus orbit, each paired with one directly sourced reason to go.

cards.title: Paint a Pottery Piece
cards.subtitle: North Decatur Road • Emory Village
cards.notes: Choose a pottery piece to paint, then confirm firing and pickup timing with the studio before planning your return trip.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on ceramics stop directly across from Emory’s campus orbit.
cards.evidence_claim: All Fired Up’s official locations page lists its Emory Village studio at 1563 North Decatur Road and identifies the business as a paint-your-own-pottery studio.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists Monday–Thursday 10 a.m.–8 p.m., Friday–Saturday 10 a.m.–10 p.m., and Sunday noon–7 p.m.; confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Settle In Beside the Coffee Bar
cards.subtitle: North Decatur Road • Emory Village
cards.notes: Use the indoor tables or outdoor seating for a compact study session, and check the official page before relying on closing time.
cards.short_summary: A corridor-side café with documented indoor and outdoor seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Summit Coffee’s official page places its Emory Village café at 1565 North Decatur Road and documents coffee, seasonal drinks, and indoor and outdoor seating.
cards.access_notes: The official page currently lists daily hours of 7 a.m.–5 p.m. and notes a shared rear lot plus nearby street parking.

cards.title: Build a Salad or Warm Bowl
cards.subtitle: North Decatur Road • Emory Village
cards.notes: Order a salad or warm bowl when you need a quick meal, and verify the location listing before making a late-evening trip.
cards.short_summary: A clearly documented fast-casual option on the village corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Sweetgreen’s official locations page lists the Emory Village restaurant at 1556 North Decatur Road.
cards.source_title: Sweetgreen Locations | Find a Restaurant Near You
cards.access_notes: The official locator lists Monday–Friday 10:30 a.m.–10 p.m. and Saturday–Sunday 10:30 a.m.–9 p.m.; hours may change.

cards.title: Choose Japanese Lunch or Dinner
cards.subtitle: North Decatur Road • Emory Village
cards.notes: Review the menu before heading over, then use the restaurant’s documented rear or nearby lot arrangements if arriving by car.
cards.short_summary: A Japanese restaurant with an Emory Village address and documented parking.
cards.evidence_claim: Wagaya’s official locations page lists its Emory Village restaurant at 1579 North Decatur Road and provides menu, ordering, and parking information.
cards.source_title: Wagaya Locations in Atlanta | Westside & Emory Village
cards.access_notes: Lunch and dinner parking instructions differ on the official page; consult it before driving. Current operating hours are not stated there.

cards.title: Restock Day-to-Day Essentials
cards.subtitle: North Decatur Road • Emory Village
cards.notes: Use this stop for household or health essentials, but check pharmacy hours separately because they differ from store hours.
cards.short_summary: A documented 24-hour retail stop with pharmacy and pickup services.
cards.evidence_claim: CVS’s official Atlanta locator lists store #4720 at 1554 North Decatur Road with in-store pickup and immunization services.
cards.source_title: CVS Near Me | Atlanta, GA | CVS Pharmacy Locations
cards.access_notes: The official locator currently marks the store and photo counter open 24 hours; the pharmacy keeps separate, shorter hours.

cards.title: Pair Natural History with a Forest Walk
cards.subtitle: Clifton Road • near Ponce de Leon Avenue
cards.notes: Reserve enough time for both the museum and outdoor areas, and review admission details before leaving the Emory area.
cards.short_summary: A natural-history museum and old-growth forest on the Clifton corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Fernbank Museum’s official directions page identifies the destination as a natural-history museum, giant-screen theater, and old-growth forest at 767 Clifton Road.
cards.source_title: Directions | Fernbank Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: The museum reports free but limited on-site parking and additional parking on South Ponce de Leon Avenue; admission requires a ticket.

cards.title: Explore the Free Exhibit Hall
cards.subtitle: Heaton Park Drive • east of Emory
cards.notes: Check the live calendar first, then visit the exhibit hall without a reservation; planetarium programs use separate tickets.
cards.short_summary: A free science exhibit hall with optional ticketed planetarium programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Fernbank Science Center’s official visitor page states that general admission and parking are free at 156 Heaton Park Drive, while planetarium admission is separate.
cards.access_notes: Hours vary during the year, and the center directs visitors to confirm its calendar. Exhibit-hall entry needs no reservation.

cards.title: Take an Arts Class or See an Exhibition
cards.subtitle: Briarcliff Road • southwest of Emory
cards.notes: Browse the current class and gallery calendars, then confirm public access because appointments are required during some periods.
cards.short_summary: A historic arts center offering classes, exhibitions, and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: Callanwolde’s official site places the center at 980 Briarcliff Road and documents classes, workshops, galleries, concerts, and events for multiple age groups.
cards.access_notes: The official contact page says public access requires an appointment during June and July; individual programs may require registration or tickets.

cards.title: Follow a Nature Trail
cards.subtitle: McConnell Drive • northeast of Emory
cards.notes: Use the county-listed nature trail or picnic area, and consult posted facility information before planning tennis or indoor recreation.
cards.short_summary: A county park combining trails, courts, fields, a lake, and picnic space.
cards.evidence_claim: DeKalb County lists Mason Mill Park facilities on McConnell Drive, including a nature trail, tennis courts, picnic area, lake, and multi-use fields.
cards.access_notes: County information lists separate recreation-center and tennis facilities; consult current facility schedules before using staffed amenities.

cards.title: Make a Full Grocery Run
cards.subtitle: LaVista Road • Toco Hills
cards.notes: Bring a complete shopping list for groceries, deli items, or pharmacy needs, and check the pharmacy’s shorter schedule separately.
cards.short_summary: A full grocery and pharmacy stop on the LaVista Road corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Kroger’s official store page lists its Toco Hills location at 2205 LaVista Road with grocery, bakery, deli, pharmacy, pickup, and other departments.
cards.source_title: Kroger Toco Hills Grocery Pickup Atlanta, GA
cards.access_notes: The official page currently lists the grocery store daily from 6 a.m.–11 p.m.; pharmacy hours are shorter and include a midday closure.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From a skeletal spirit who dismisses classes to residence-hall songs and a Coca-Cola welcome, these documented rituals mark the Emory calendar.

cards.title: When a Skeleton Dismisses Class
cards.subtitle: Emory’s resident spirit presides over a spring week of events
cards.notes: Watch for Lord Dooley and his entourage; bring a well-written limerick if you hope the university’s skeletal spirit will dismiss your class.
cards.short_summary: A costumed skeleton with a century-old campus persona becomes Emory’s unofficial authority for one spring week.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory identifies Dooley’s Week as a spring tradition hosted by the Student Programming Council, and says Dooley may cancel a class in exchange for a well-written limerick.
cards.access_notes: Participation and class-dismissal appearances depend on the current Dooley’s Week program.

cards.title: Wednesday Gets Its Own Campus Festival
cards.subtitle: Student groups take over the middle of the week
cards.notes: Walk through the scheduled gathering and browse the student-group tables; programming changes weekly, so check the university calendar first.
cards.short_summary: Emory turns an ordinary weekday into a recurring showcase for student organizations, activities and campus connection.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory describes Wonderful Wednesday as a weekly event where student groups showcase what is happening, and its 2025 history traces the tradition’s evolution and revival.
cards.source_title: Magic of Midweek: The Evolution of Wonderful Wednesday
cards.access_notes: Consult Emory’s events calendar for the date, location and participation details of a particular week.

cards.title: Residence Halls Rewrite the Hits
cards.subtitle: First-years sing and dance for hall pride
cards.notes: Cheer for a residence hall or join its rehearsals if eligible; each team performs new lyrics and choreography set to familiar tunes.
cards.short_summary: Days after arriving, first-years turn residence-hall identity into a student-led musical competition.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory reports that Songfest began in 1984 and features first-year residence halls competing with original lyrics and choreography set to popular songs.
cards.source_title: Songfest celebrates 40th anniversary as beloved Emory tradition
cards.access_notes: Performance participation is for first-year residence halls; audience arrangements can vary by year.

cards.title: Enter Through the Gate, Then Raise a Coke
cards.subtitle: The incoming class crosses Emory’s threshold together
cards.notes: Line the route to cheer for incoming students, then follow the procession toward the Quad for the class’s first Coca-Cola toast.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial walk through the Haygood-Hopkins Gate leads directly into Emory’s orientation toast.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory’s 2024 fall guide says the Class of 2028 would cross the Emory gate, proceed to the Quad and participate in its first Coke Toast.
cards.source_title: 10 things to know for fall semester at Emory
cards.access_notes: The procession is tied to fall orientation; use the current welcome schedule for that year’s route and timing.

cards.title: Seniors Cross Over by Candlelight
cards.subtitle: A procession marks the shift from student to alum
cards.notes: Join the senior procession after finals and carry the ceremonial moment from the Emory Student Center toward the Quadrangle.
cards.short_summary: Graduating seniors physically cross campus together as their student chapter closes and alumni status begins.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory’s 2026 guide says seniors cross from students to alumni in a candlelight procession from the Emory Student Center to the Quadrangle after finals.
cards.source_title: From Speeches in Latin to Social Media Posts: A Guide to Emory’s Evolving Commencement Traditions
cards.access_notes: Held for graduating seniors before Commencement; the outdoor procession is weather permitting.

cards.title: Faculty Flip the Finals Script
cards.subtitle: Oxford instructors serve a late-night pancake meal
cards.notes: Take a study break at the announced finals meal and let Oxford faculty and staff handle the pancake service for the night.
cards.short_summary: During finals, the usual academic roles soften over stacks of pancakes served late at night.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory’s campus-culture page identifies Midnight Pancakes as a late-night finals meal served to Oxford College students by faculty and staff.
cards.access_notes: This Oxford College finals tradition is for students; confirm the semester’s date and entry details through campus announcements.

cards.title: The First Day Ends at a Carnival
cards.subtitle: Classes begin, then the Quad fills with rides and games
cards.notes: After the first day of classes, head to the announced Quad program for carnival rides, games, music and fair-style food.
cards.short_summary: Emory answers the first day’s academic intensity with a student-programmed evening carnival.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory lists First Day Fest among its campus traditions and describes it as a first-day-of-classes carnival on the Quad with rides, games, music and fair-style food.
cards.access_notes: The event is scheduled around the first day of fall classes; verify current timing and attendance rules before going.

cards.title: One Bell Toll for Every Oxford Graduate
cards.subtitle: Commencement ends with a name-by-name count in sound
cards.notes: Remain after the Oxford recessional to hear the historic Seney Hall bell mark the graduating class one student at a time.
cards.short_summary: Oxford College translates its graduating-class roster into individual tolls from its historic bell.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory’s 2026 Commencement traditions guide says the historic Seney Hall bell tolls once for each Oxford College graduating student after the recessional.
cards.source_title: From Speeches in Latin to Social Media Posts: A Guide to Emory’s Evolving Commencement Traditions
cards.access_notes: This occurs as part of Oxford College’s graduation ceremony; ceremony access requirements apply.

cards.title: Sign “MD” for the First Time
cards.subtitle: New physicians add their names during hooding
cards.notes: During the School of Medicine hooding ceremony, watch for graduates to enter the alumni book using their new credential.
cards.short_summary: Emory medical graduates make their new professional title tangible with a ceremonial signature.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory says School of Medicine graduates sign the MD program alumni book during hooding, using the MD credential for the first time, a tradition dating to 1992.
cards.source_title: From Speeches in Latin to Social Media Posts: A Guide to Emory’s Evolving Commencement Traditions
cards.access_notes: Participation is limited to graduating MD students during the School of Medicine hooding ceremony.

cards.entity_name: Society of Corpus Cordis Aureum Procession
cards.title: Golden Eagles Lead the Graduates
cards.subtitle: Fifty-year alumni return in gold robes
cards.notes: At Commencement, look for alumni from classes of 50 or more years ago processing in gold ahead of the degree candidates.
cards.short_summary: Emory’s longest-tenured alumni visibly lead its newest graduates into Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory’s 2026 traditions guide says Society of Corpus Cordis Aureum members are alumni of 50 or more years who wear gold robes and lead degree candidates in the Commencement procession.
cards.source_title: From Speeches in Latin to Social Media Posts: A Guide to Emory’s Evolving Commencement Traditions
cards.access_notes: Procession participation is for eligible Society members; Commencement access requirements apply to observers.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Emory University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A conservative Friday-to-Sunday introduction to Emory’s Atlanta campus, combining practical orientation stops, meals, study spaces, recreation, art, and outdoor landmarks.

cards.title: Friday Arrival: Find Emory’s Front Door
cards.subtitle: Begin at the Haygood-Hopkins Gate before walking toward the Quad
cards.notes: Read the inscription at the historic gate, photograph the marble pillars, then follow the brick walk toward the university’s central Quad.
cards.short_summary: Use Emory’s original Atlanta-campus entrance as a clear starting point for learning the central-campus layout.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory identifies Haygood-Hopkins Gate as the original entrance to its Atlanta campus and documents it as the site of the first-year Gate Crossing tradition.
cards.access_notes: This card proposes viewing the outdoor gate, not reenacting the school’s scheduled Gate Crossing ceremony.

cards.title: Friday Check-In: Learn the Student Center
cards.subtitle: Locate the Welcome Desk and the building’s main gathering spaces
cards.notes: Stop at the second-floor Welcome Desk for a campus map, directions, resource information, and details about upcoming student events.
cards.short_summary: Make the campus union your practical base for maps, questions, meeting rooms, dining, and student programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory describes the Student Center as the Atlanta campus student union and says its Welcome Desk supplies directions, resource information, event information, brochures, and campus maps.
cards.access_notes: Posted public building hours are Monday–Friday 7 a.m.–10 p.m. and Saturday–Sunday 8 a.m.–10 p.m.; Emory students have 24-hour EmoryCard access.

cards.title: Friday Dinner: Try the Residential Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: Eat inside the Emory Student Center before the evening continues
cards.notes: Use your dining plan for a full meal, and review the posted stations and dietary choices before deciding what fits your needs.
cards.short_summary: Start the weekend with a straightforward meal at Emory’s primary residential dining facility.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory Dining identifies Dobbs Common Table, on the first floor of ESC South, as an all-you-care-to-eat dining hall where students can use their dining plans.
cards.access_notes: Located at 605 Asbury Circle. Check Emory Dining’s current-hours PDF because schedules change during breaks and holidays.

cards.title: Friday Sunset: Walk the Quad
cards.subtitle: Trace the central green and its marble academic buildings
cards.notes: Walk one easy circuit, identify the surrounding academic buildings, and note the route back toward your residence before nightfall.
cards.short_summary: A short Quad circuit establishes the visual center of Emory’s Atlanta campus without requiring a scheduled activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory’s campus design guidance calls the Quadrangle the historic soul of campus, while its walking guide identifies the Quad as an easy walking location in the heart of the main campus.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and campus operations can change; use Emory’s interactive map for current wayfinding.

cards.title: Saturday Morning: Map Your Library
cards.subtitle: Tour the main building’s service points and study areas
cards.notes: Enter with your Emory ID, locate the Level 2 service desk, and identify one study space you can return to during the semester.
cards.short_summary: A brief self-guided library visit turns a large academic building into a familiar, usable resource.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory Libraries says Woodruff Library houses multiple libraries, service points, academic technologies, collections, and study spaces at 540 Asbury Court.
cards.access_notes: Current students should carry an Emory ID. Access may be restricted during reading and examination periods; verify the live hours page before going.

cards.title: Saturday Midday: Browse the Carlos Museum
cards.subtitle: Choose one collection for a focused first visit
cards.notes: Bring your student ID, check large bags at the Level One desk, and spend the visit closely examining one gallery rather than rushing.
cards.short_summary: Use complimentary student admission for a manageable introduction to Emory’s campus museum collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Carlos Museum lists free admission for college and university students with valid ID and publishes regular Tuesday-through-Sunday hours.
cards.source_title: Hours and Admission | Emory Carlos Museum
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday noon–5 p.m.; closed Mondays and university holidays. Bring valid student ID.

cards.title: Saturday Afternoon: Explore Cox Hall
cards.subtitle: Connect dining, study lounges, computing, and creative facilities
cards.notes: Walk through the first-floor market area, then find the second-floor lounges and computing spaces for a quick campus-resources preview.
cards.short_summary: Cox Hall combines several everyday student functions in one centrally located building near Asbury Circle.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory describes Cox Hall as a central place for dining, studying, and community, with a food market, second-floor lounges, a Computing Center, and an Arts and Tech Lab.
cards.access_notes: Posted building hours are Saturday–Sunday 8 a.m.–10 p.m. Dining and Computing Center schedules are separate and may change.

cards.title: Saturday Outdoors: Follow a Lullwater Route
cards.subtitle: Take a daylight walk through the campus preserve
cards.notes: Choose a marked route, stay on established trails, carry water, and turn back early enough to leave the preserve before dark.
cards.short_summary: Add a daylight nature break using Emory’s documented walking routes through its wooded campus preserve.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory identifies Lullwater Preserve as a 154-acre area with walking routes, trees, green space, a lake, and Lullwater House.
cards.access_notes: Visit in daylight, remain on established routes, and check weather and campus alerts. Emory lists entrances near 1463 Clifton Road and Clairmont campus.

cards.title: Sunday Morning: Try the SAAC
cards.subtitle: Explore recreation and study facilities on the Clairmont campus
cards.notes: Carry your Emory ID, check in at the front desk, and ask which student recreation spaces are open before choosing an activity.
cards.short_summary: Learn the Clairmont campus recreation hub through a low-pressure visit that can include study or physical activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory says the SAAC contains indoor and outdoor recreation facilities, classrooms, study space, a computer lab, café, mail center, and Accessibility Services.
cards.access_notes: Students must present an Emory ID. Verify current facility hours and availability; some facilities or reservations have separate rules and charges.

cards.entity_name: Donna and Marvin Schwartz Center for Performing Arts
cards.title: Sunday Afternoon: Scout the Schwartz Center
cards.subtitle: Learn the entrances, venues, and event-checking routine
cards.notes: Find the main lobby and Allen Plaza entrances, review the events calendar, and save one suitable performance for a later visit.
cards.short_summary: Close the weekend by learning where Emory’s principal performance venues and arts box office are located.
cards.evidence_claim: Emory’s visitor page places Emerson Concert Hall, the Dance Studio, Chace Gallery, Theater Lab, and Tharp Rehearsal Hall within the Schwartz Center.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Schwartz Center for Performing Arts
cards.access_notes: Venue access depends on scheduled events. Check the official calendar and ticket requirements before entering performance spaces.
